Iran has denied responsibility for the attack, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying the incident looked "suspicious" and that Tehran would work with Kuwait and Italy to "determine the cause". It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country. Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war. On Thursday, Araghchi said he had expressed condolences over the deaths in calls with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts and that the incident looked like a "precooked recipe for war", without expanding further. clusters.text: Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another election The final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls. Preliminary results on 7 November handed the National party and its two coalition partners, the populist New Zealand First and libertarian Act parties, a slim two-seat majority, making the election too close to call until final votes were tallied. On Friday, the electoral commission released the results from nearly 485,000 “special votes” – those cast from overseas or outside a voter’s electorate. National dropped two seats to 40, Labour stayed on 36 seats, the Greens picked up one seat to 17, Act had 13, New Zealand First 12, Opportunity seven and Te Pati Māori five. The National-led bloc currently has 65 seats. In the 130-seat parliament, 66 seats are needed for a majority. The revised results mean the National-led coalition has the only realistic path to power – if it can negotiate a deal with Opportunity. If it cannot, New Zealand will probably need to hold another election. Three electorate seats changed hands after the special votes. Labour won Wairarapa off National with just 81 votes, and took Hamilton East from National with 173 votes. The Greens won Wellington Bays from Labour with 1,610 votes. If National applies for a recount and wins back just one of those seats, it could return to power with a slim majority and without needing Opportunity. Applications for a recount must be made by 3 December, and results could take another five days. Special votes in previous elections have favoured the left, and typically have cost the right one or two seats. Until Friday, a question mark hung over whether National would be able to govern comfortably alongside its coalition partners, or whether it would be forced to cut a deal with the Opportunity party – a newcomer centrist party that incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon had previously ruled out working with. The first-half problem was clearest when Fede Valverde made a run beyond his marker. Madrid could open the passing lane, but too often the next pass went backwards. The numbers by half give some indication of how different the two performances were. In the seventh minute, Valverde drifts inside, taking Van Bommel with him and opening a passing lane from Éder Militão to Yan Diomandé on the right touchline. Diomandé plays back to Aurélien Tchouaméni, and Madrid settle into possession. clusters.text: Agentic offensive framework automates familiar attack techniques, with weak defenses potentially breached in minutes Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. clusters.text: Prayagraj(UP), Nov 26 (PTI) The Allahabad High Court on Thursday set aside the election of BJP MLA Om Kumar over anomalies in his nomination paper. Kumar was elected to the assembly from Nehtaur (Reserved - Scheduled Caste) constituency in Bijnor after he defeated RLD’s Munshi Ram by 258 votes. The elections were held on February 14, 2022 and the results were declared on March 10, 2022. Justice Salil Kumar Rai, partly allowing the election petition filed by Munshi Ram, however, stayed the operation of order for 15 days to some extent. “It is directed that for a period of fifteen days counted from today, the respondent Om Kumar shall be entitled to represent the electorate of his constituency and to participate in the debates of the Vidhan Sabha if any held during the period of fifteen days,” the court said. “However, he shall not be entitled to cast his vote on the floor of Vidhan Sabha or in any committee of the Vidhan Sabha. He shall also not be entitled to any monetary benefits as a member of the Vidhan Sabha.” The court also observed, “It is held that the affidavit in Form 26 filed by Om Kumar suffered from a defect of substantial character, requiring rejection of his nomination paper under Section 36(2) read with Section 36(4) of Representation of People Act.” It went on to add, “His (Om Kumar) nomination paper was therefore improperly accepted by the returning officer and the improper acceptance of the nomination materially affected the result of his election.” However, the court did not accept allegations regarding irregularities in counting of votes and said, “It is held that the petitioner has failed to prove any illegality or irregularity in the counting of VVPAT slips relating to polling booth Nos. 44, 54, 180 and 234, or that any such irregularity materially affected the election result in so far as it concerns respondent no. 1, the returned candidate.” It also said, “There is no cogent or reliable evidence to establish that the votes obtained by Om Kumar would have been cast in favour of the petitioner if Kumar had not contested the election. clusters.title: NUSRL Ranchi Organises National Symposium on Constitution Day
clusters.text: The National University of Study and Research in Law (NUSRL), Ranchi, organised a National Symposium on Constitution Day on Thursday. The theme was “Constitutional Values, Fundamental Duties and National Unity”, under the broader message “Our Constitution, Our Pride”. The symposium was organised on 26 November 2026 to commemorate the 77th anniversary of the adoption of the Constitution of India. The programme was graced by Shri Sanjay Seth, Hon’ble Minister of State for Defence, Government of India, as the Chief Guest. The programme commenced with the arrival of the dignitary, followed by tree plantation, symbolising the University's commitment to environmental responsibility. The ceremony further included the lighting of the ceremonial lamp and felicitation of the Chief Guest. The dignitaries on the dais included Shri Sanjay Seth, Hon’ble Minister of State for Defence, Prof. (Dr.) Ashok R. Patil, Vice-Chancellor, NUSRL Ranchi and Prof. (Dr.) Dharmender Patial, Registrar, NUSRL Ranchi. Faculty members, university officials, research scholars, students and other distinguished guests were also present on the occasion. Delivering the welcome address, Vice-Chancellor Prof. (Dr.) Ashok R. Patil highlighted the significance of Constitution Day and the responsibilities that accompany constitutional rights. He observed that while Fundamental Rights are essential pillars of democracy, the Fundamental Duties enshrined under Article 51A remind citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation and fellow citizens. Referring to the Constituent Assembly debates and Jharkhand's contribution to the making of the Constitution, the Vice-Chancellor particularly recalled the role of Jaipal Singh Munda in raising the voice and aspirations of Adivasi communities. He emphasised that India's constitutional framework reflects the participation and aspirations of people from every corner of the country. Explaining the relationship between Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties, Prof. Patil stated that rights define what citizens can claim, while duties determine how they contribute to ensuring those rights for everyone. Referring to Dr. B. R. Ambedkar's vision, he highlighted the inseparable relationship between liberty, equality and fraternity. clusters.title: Jharkhand: Five girls rescued from trafficking at Ranchi station
clusters.text: The Railway Protection Force rescued five girls here who were allegedly being trafficked to Tamil Nadu on the pretext of employment at a spinning mill, officials said on Friday. Acting on a tip-off, a team comprising personnel from the RPF and its Crime Intelligence Branch (CIB) intercepted a 41-year-old man on Thursday, after the Sasaram-Intercity Express arrived at Ranchi railway station, they said. The rescued girls, aged between 16 and 17 years, hail from Garhwa and Palamu districts. The man, who has been arrested, is a resident of Upper Khurd village in Palamu district, a senior officer said. “During interrogation, the man told investigators that he works as a supervisor at a spinning mill in Tamil Nadu, and trafficked girls after luring them with jobs at the firm, offering a monthly salary of Rs 15,000 each," said Shishupal Singh, officer in-charge at RPF police station, Ranchi. clusters.title: INTACH Prayagraj concludes Heritage Week celebrations
clusters.text: Prayagraj: The INTACH Prayagraj Chapter concluded its Heritage Week celebrations from Nov 19 to 25 with four programmes showcasing the city and region’s architectural, cultural and intangible heritage.The initiative included heritage walks, a panel discussion, a photography exhibition and a full-day heritage walk in Kaushambi.The celebrations included a culinary heritage walk through the historic Loknath area, where participants explored Prayagraj’s traditional food culture and sampled local delicacies such as papdi chaat, pudina aloo, Hari ke samose and fruit cream. The walk was led by Adarsh Malviya.Later, a panel discussion at Allahabad Fort focused on the monument’s architectural, cultural and social evolution and its role in shaping Prayagraj’s history.INTACH Prayagraj Chapter secretary Vaibhav Maini spoke on the fort’s historical development, while Adarsh Malviya discussed the cultural significance of Dussehra in Prayagraj, particularly during the freedom movement. The Fort Commandant also shared insights into the monument’s legacy and appreciated INTACH’s conservation outreach.The Heritage Week concluded with a full-day walk across Kaushambi covering the Ashokan Pillar, Ghositaram Vihara, Udayana Fort and Pabhosa Hill.

clusters.title: Statehood Day fair showcases culture, devpt
clusters.text: Ranchi: Jharkhand’s cultural colours, local flavours and development initiatives came together at Khelgaon on Thursday as a three-day Statehood Day fair-cum-exhibition opened, bringing the city alive with folk performances and other attractions. The fair, which is open till Saturday, is part of the statehood fortnight celebrations and will culminate in the main programme marking the state govt's second anniversary.The opening day's cultural programme featured Mundari, Oraon, Nagpuri and Santhali dance performances, along with Chhau, showcasing the diversity of Jharkhand’s tribal and folk traditions. Dancers in traditional attire performed to folk rhythms, drawing visitors towards the cultural arena.Minister Dipika Pandey Singh, who inaugurated the event, said Jharkhand’s rich cultural heritage and development journey must reach every household, and this exhibition provides a platform to showcase both.The exhibition has pavilions representing all 24 districts, alongside departmental and innovation-focused stalls. The displays showcase govt schemes, public services, district-specific products, tourism destinations, economic activities and initiatives involving new technologies, research, IT services and sports apparel.A food court serving traditional delicacies such as ‘dhuska’, ‘ghughni’, ‘pitha’ and ‘chhilka roti’ is also among the attractions.For visitors, the cultural performances offered a chance to experience traditions from across the state without travelling to different regions.“The dance performances were the most interesting element of the day. Each community has a distinct style, costume and music. It feels like experiencing Jharkhand in one place,” said Anjali Sinha, a visitor.The fair will continue with cultural programmes on Friday and Saturday.Friday's major attraction is scheduled to be a live performance by Sunidhi Chauhan, while the concluding day will feature the main state-level celebrations, project inaugurations and foundation-laying, asset distribution among beneficiaries and felicitation of achievers.
